headline: High-risk data leakage and capability conflict: Plandex’s writable shell/filesystem can collide with Kotaemon’s broad API/file handling and secret-bearing workspace.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Kotaemon ingests HTML, PDFs, DOCX, chat transcripts, and files in ./ktem_app_data, while Plandex reads/writes a project directory and plan-local sandbox. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if Kotaemon outputs are copied into Plandex or vice versa. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is not high.
conditions: IF Kotaemon outputs are pasted into Plandex plans without review, prompt injection is possible.
IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace files, attacker-controlled content can cross from one agent to the other.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate directories.
Disable auto-apply in Plandex.
Manually review any text copied from Kotaemon before pasting into Plandex.
Use a read-only export step for Kotaemon outputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between the two tools.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Kotaemon handles API keys and broad document types, and Plandex has read/write filesystem access plus broad network egress. If they share a workspace, Plandex can read sensitive files and transmit context to model providers or its server. That is a realistic exfiltration path in default-style use, so the blast radius is severe.
conditions: IF both agents are run against the same project or app-data directory, Plandex can read Kotaemon-managed secrets or documents.
IF Plandex sends plan context to a model provider or Plandex Cloud, copied sensitive content can leave the local machine.
mitigations: Place Kotaemon and Plandex in separate workspaces.
Remove secrets from any shared directory before running Plandex.
Use local-only model endpoints where possible.
Restrict Plandex to non-sensitive files.
requires-engineering: enforce filesystem ACL separation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Plandex can execute shell commands, modify git state, and write the filesystem; Kotaemon also supports multiple instances and broad network egress, but no locking or coordination is documented. If both touch the same repo or workspace, concurrent edits and git mutations can overwrite each other or corrupt state. Uncertainty about orchestration means we should choose the higher severity.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git repository, concurrent writes can conflict.
IF Kotaemon is used to generate or transform files while Plandex applies patches, git state can diverge without locks.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate repo clone.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Disable auto-apply in Plandex.
Use git branches per agent.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plandex is a planner with review-then-apply and optional auto-apply, so it may treat Kotaemon-produced text as input to code changes or shell actions. Kotaemon can generate document-derived outputs, but no direct action authority is shown. The pathway exists, but Plandex’s review step reduces the risk below high.
conditions: IF Kotaemon outputs are used as authoritative specs, Plandex may implement incorrect changes.
IF Plandex auto-apply is enabled, unverified downstream actions can occur.
mitigations: Require human review before apply.
Cross-check Kotaemon outputs against source documents.
Keep auto-apply disabled.
Limit Plandex to low-risk branches.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before execution.

E_compliance.rationale: Kotaemon explicitly handles API keys and chat transcripts, while Plandex uses a cloud or self-hosted server and model providers. If regulated or sensitive content from Kotaemon is routed into Plandex Cloud or external model APIs, retention and residency obligations may diverge. The profiles do not specify a concrete jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the safest supported level.
conditions: IF Kotaemon processes regulated documents and Plandex forwards them to external model providers, compliance obligations may be breached.
IF the deployment uses Plandex Cloud for data that must remain local, residency/retention mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Plandex inputs.
Use self-hosted or local model endpoints.
Review retention settings for both tools.
Separate sensitive and non-sensitive workflows.
requires-engineering: document a data-processing agreement and residency controls.
